question: What is the very first step of the nursing process in clinical practice?
explanation: Assessment forms the foundational first step upon which all other nursing actions depend. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why do midwives treat assessment as a continuous activity rather than something done just once?

options.A: Midwives have spare time during night shifts to update charts
options.B: Doctors refuse to review patients who lack hourly updates
options.C: A woman's clinical condition and needs can change rapidly during labor
options.D: Hospital regulations require rewriting admission notes every shift

explanation: Maternity conditions are dynamic, meaning a stable mother can develop complications quickly, requiring continuous reassessment. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h1)

question: Which of the following is a clear example of subjective data?

options.A: A positive result on a malaria rapid test
options.B: A pregnant woman complaining of dizziness
options.C: A fetal heart rate of 140 beats per minute
options.D: A blood pressure reading of 140/90 mmHg

explanation: Subjective data consists of what the patient feels and reports herself, such as dizziness. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h2)

question: A woman says she feels her baby moving less today, but your physical check shows a normal fetal heart rate. How should you view her report of reduced movement?

options.A: Objective data because it involves the fetus
options.B: Unreliable data that can be safely ignored
options.C: Subjective data that requires serious attention
options.D: Secondary data obtained from a relative

explanation: A patient's personal description of her symptoms is always classified as subjective data, regardless of objective test findings. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which physical examination method is used to listen to internal body sounds like the fetal heartbeat?
explanation: Auscultation is the act of listening to internal sounds using tools like a stethoscope or Fetoscope. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is building a friendly connection with a pregnant woman during her interview so important in midwifery?

options.A: It is a legal requirement before taking her temperature
options.B: It shortens the time needed to complete the antenatal register
options.C: It encourages her to share accurate and sensitive health information freely
options.D: It prevents her from asking questions about her bill

explanation: Trusting relationships reduce anxiety and help mothers disclose vital details about their health and social background. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h3)

question: What is the main goal of double-checking assessment data before making a care plan?

options.A: To satisfy hospital audit requirements for billing
options.B: To prevent clinical errors caused by inaccurate or misunderstood information
options.C: To ensure two different midwives sign off on the patient folder
options.D: To delay treatment until a senior doctor arrives

explanation: Validation double-checks information to make sure nursing decisions are based on true facts rather than mistakes or temporary errors. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h4)

question: You measure a high temperature in a woman in labor, but she feels cool to the touch and says she feels fine. What is the best next step?

options.A: Repeat the temperature measurement to validate the finding
options.B: Assume the thermometer is broken and ignore the reading
options.C: Record the fever in the chart and start cooling measures

explanation: When subjective feelings contradict objective readings, validating the measurement helps rule out equipment error or improper technique. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h4)

question: Which of the following describes an acceptable standard for clinical documentation?

options.D: Delayed until the end of the work week

explanation: Good records must state exact facts, be written promptly, and describe specific clinical observations clearly. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h5)

question: Why is the saying "if it was not documented, it was not done" stressed so much in midwifery training?

options.A: Hospital management uses notes to calculate daily staff wages
options.B: Unwritten notes are automatically uploaded to public databases
options.C: Courts and professional boards rely solely on written records as proof of care
options.D: Patients check their folders daily to verify midwife attendance

explanation: In legal investigations, written documentation is the only recognized legal evidence that a proper assessment and intervention took place. [learn more](BMP120_U1_T2#BMP120_U1_T2_h5)
